ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, point D and E are on $\odot O$, and quadrilateral BDEO is a parallelogram. A line through point D, $DC\perp AE$, intersects the extension of AE at point C. CD is the tangent of $\odot O$. If $AC=9$, what is the area of the shaded region?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given (1) we have $\angle EAO = \angle AOE = \angle OBD = \angle BOD = 60^\circ$, and $ED \parallel AB$,

$\therefore \angle EAO = \angle CED = 60^\circ$,

$\because \angle AOE + \angle EOD + \angle BOD = 180^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle EOD = 60^\circ$,

$\therefore \triangle DEO$ is an equilateral triangle,

$\therefore ED = OE = AE$,

$\because CD \perp AE$, $\angle CED = 60^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle CDE = 30^\circ$,

$\therefore ED = 2CE = AE$,

$\because AC = 9$,

$\therefore CE = 3$, $AE = OE = ED = 6$,

$\therefore CD = \sqrt{ED^2 - CE^2} = 3\sqrt{3}$,

Let the height of $\triangle OED$ be $h$,

$\therefore h = OE \cdot \sin 60^\circ = 3\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore S_{\text{sector} ED} = S_{\text{sector} OED} - S_{\triangle OED} = \frac{\pi r^{2}n}{360}-\frac{1}{2}ED\cdot h = 6\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore S_{\text{shaded area}} = S_{\triangle CED} - S_{\text{arc} ED} = \frac{1}{2}CE \cdot CD - (6\pi - 9\sqrt{3}) = \boxed{\frac{27\sqrt{3}}{2} - 6\pi}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, AB is the horizontal diameter, and O is at the midpoint of AB; E and D are both on the upper semicircle, and ED is an approximately horizontal chord; C is on the extension of E and located outside the circle, CD is perpendicular to AE, and at the same time CD is tangent to the circle; the shaded part is the upper small cap region enclosed by CE, CD, and arc ED, that is, △CED minus the circular segment between chord ED and arc ED. Then reason: Because BDEO is a parallelogram, BD∥EO, DE∥BO, and BD=EO, DE=BO. Also OB, OD, and OE are all radii of the same circle, so OB=OD=OE=BO=DE=BD=r; therefore △OBD and △ODE are both equilateral triangles, giving ∠BOD=∠EOD=60°. Also A, O, and B are collinear, so ∠AOE=180°-60°-60°=60°, and thus △AOE is also an equilateral triangle, giving AE=OE=ED=r and ∠EAO=60°. Since C is on the extension of AE, and DE∥AB∥AO, ∠CED=∠EAO=60°; also CD⊥AE, so ∠ECD=90°, hence △CED is a 30-60-90 triangle, satisfying ED=2CE and CD=\sqrt{3}\,CE. By the tangent-secant theorem, for the external point C to tangent CD and secant CEA there is CD^2=CE\cdot CA=9CE. On the other hand, because CD=\sqrt{3}\,CE, CD^2=3CE^2. Combining gives 3CE^2=9CE, so CE=3, and then CD=3\sqrt{3}, ED=6, so the circle radius r=6. Shaded area = area of △CED - area of circular segment ED. Area of △CED = \frac12\cdot CE\cdot CD=\frac12\cdot3\cdot3\sqrt{3}=\frac{9\sqrt{3}}2. The central angle corresponding to arc ED is 60°, so area of sector OED = \frac{60}{360}\pi\cdot6^2=6\pi; area of △OED = \frac12\cdot6^2\sin60°=9\sqrt{3}. Therefore the area of the circular segment = 6\pi-9\sqrt{3}. Thus the shaded area = \frac{9\sqrt{3}}2-(6\pi-9\sqrt{3})=\frac{27\sqrt{3}}2-6\pi.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: AB is the horizontal diameter with O at its midpoint, E and D lie on the upper semicircle, ED is a horizontal chord, C is above the circle on the extension of AE, and the shaded region is triangle CED with the circular segment between chord ED and arc ED removed. The parallelogram also gives ED parallel OB, so the chord ED subtends central angle EOD=60° and ED equals the radius. Also CE lies along AE and CD is perpendicular to AE, so triangle CED is right; with angle CED=60°, it is a 30-60-90 triangle, so CD=sqrt(3)·CE and ED=2CE. Instead of finding CE from AC=AE+CE, use the tangent-secant theorem from external point C: CD^2=CE·CA=9CE. Combining with CD^2=3CE^2 gives CE=3, hence CD=3sqrt(3), ED=6, and the circle radius is 6. method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中AB是水平直径，O在AB中点；E、D都在上半圆上，ED是一条近似水平的弦；C在E的延长线上并位于圆外，CD与AE垂直，同时CD与圆相切；阴影部分是由CE、CD和弧ED围成的上方小帽区域，也就是△CED减去弦ED与弧ED之间的圆弓形。
再推理：因为BDEO是平行四边形，所以BD∥EO，DE∥BO，且BD=EO、DE=BO。又OB、OD、OE都是同一圆的半径，所以OB=OD=OE=BO=DE=BD=r，因此△OBD和△ODE都为等边三角形，得到∠BOD=∠EOD=60°。又A、O、B共线，所以∠AOE=180°-60°-60°=60°，从而△AOE也是等边三角形，得到AE=OE=ED=r，且∠EAO=60°。由于C在AE延长线上，且DE∥AB∥AO，所以∠CED=∠EAO=60°；又CD⊥AE，所以∠ECD=90°，故△CED为30-60-90三角形，满足ED=2CE，CD=\sqrt{3}\,CE。
由切割线定理，外点C到切线CD与割线CEA有CD^2=CE\cdot CA=9CE。另一方面，因CD=\sqrt{3}\,CE，所以CD^2=3CE^2。联立得3CE^2=9CE，故CE=3，进而CD=3\sqrt{3}，ED=6，所以圆半径r=6。
阴影面积=△CED面积-圆弓形ED面积。△CED面积=\frac12\cdot CE\cdot CD=\frac12\cdot3\cdot3\sqrt{3}=\frac{9\sqrt{3}}2。弧ED对应的圆心角为60°，所以扇形OED面积=\frac{60}{360}\pi\cdot6^2=6\pi；△OED面积=\frac12\cdot6^2\sin60°=9\sqrt{3}。故圆弓形面积=6\pi-9\sqrt{3}。于是阴影面积=\frac{9\sqrt{3}}2-(6\pi-9\sqrt{3})=\frac{27\sqrt{3}}2-6\pi。

再推理：因为BDEO是平行四边形，所以BD∥EO，DE∥BO，且BD=EO、DE=BO。又OB、OD、OE都是同一圆的半径，所以OB=OD=OE=BO=DE=BD=r，因此△OBD和△ODE都为等边三角形，得到∠BOD=∠EOD=60°。又A、O、B共线，所以∠AOE=180°-60°-60°=60°，从而△AOE也是等边三角形，得到AE=OE=ED=r，且∠EAO=60°。由于C在AE延长线上，且DE∥AB∥AO，所以∠CED=∠EAO=60°；又CD⊥AE，所以∠ECD=90°，故△CED为30-60-90三角形，满足ED=2CE，CD=\sqrt{3}\,CE。
由切割线定理，外点C到切线CD与割线CEA有CD^2=CE\cdot CA=9CE。另一方面，因CD=\sqrt{3}\,CE，所以CD^2=3CE^2。联立得3CE^2=9CE，故CE=3，进而CD=3\sqrt{3}，ED=6，所以圆半径r=6。
阴影面积=△CED面积-圆弓形ED面积。△CED面积=\frac12\cdot CE\cdot CD=\frac12\cdot3\cdot3\sqrt{3}=\frac{9\sqrt{3}}2。弧ED对应的圆心角为60°，所以扇形OED面积=\frac{60}{360}\pi\cdot6^2=6\pi；△OED面积=\frac12\cdot6^2\sin60°=9\sqrt{3}。故圆弓形面积=6\pi-9\sqrt{3}。于是阴影面积=\frac{9\sqrt{3}}2-(6\pi-9\sqrt{3})=\frac{27\sqrt{3}}2-6\pi。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, points D and E are on $\odot O$, and quadrilateral BDEO is a parallelogram. A line through point D, with $DC \perp AE$, intersects the extension of AE at point C. CD is the tangent of $\odot O$. If $AC=9$, what is the area of the shaded region?
raw_record.answer:
Solution:

Given (1) we have $\angle EAO = \angle AOE = \angle OBD = \angle BOD = 60^\circ$, and $ED \parallel AB$,

$\therefore \angle EAO = \angle CED = 60^\circ$,

$\because \angle AOE + \angle EOD + \angle BOD = 180^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle EOD = 60^\circ$,

$\therefore \triangle DEO$ is an equilateral triangle,

$\therefore ED = OE = AE$,

$\because CD \perp AE$, $\angle CED = 60^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle CDE = 30^\circ$,

$\therefore ED = 2CE = AE$,

$\because AC = 9$,

$\therefore CE = 3$, $AE = OE = ED = 6$,

$\therefore CD = \sqrt{ED^2 - CE^2} = 3\sqrt{3}$,

Let the height of $\triangle OED$ be $h$,

$\therefore h = OE \cdot \sin 60^\circ = 3\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore S_{\text{sector} ED} = S_{\text{sector} OED} - S_{\triangle OED} = \frac{\pi r^{2}n}{360}-\frac{1}{2}ED\cdot h = 6\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore S_{\text{shaded area}} = S_{\triangle CED} - S_{\text{arc} ED} = \frac{1}{2}CE \cdot CD - (6\pi - 9\sqrt{3}) = \boxed{\frac{27\sqrt{3}}{2} - 6\pi}$

Then reason: Because BDEO is a parallelogram, BD∥EO, DE∥BO, and BD=EO, DE=BO. Also OB, OD, and OE are all radii of the same circle, so OB=OD=OE=BO=DE=BD=r; therefore △OBD and △ODE are both equilateral triangles, giving ∠BOD=∠EOD=60°. By the tangent-secant theorem, for the external point C to tangent CD and secant CEA there is CD^2=CE\cdot CA=9CE. On the other hand, because CD=\sqrt{3}\,CE, CD^2=3CE^2. Combining gives 3CE^2=9CE, so CE=3, and then CD=3\sqrt{3}, ED=6, so the circle radius r=6.
Shaded area = area of △CED - area of circular segment ED. Area of △CED = \frac12\cdot CE\cdot CD=\frac12\cdot3\cdot3\sqrt{3}=\frac{9\sqrt{3}}2. The central angle corresponding to arc ED is 60°, so area of sector OED = \frac{60}{360}\pi\cdot6^2=6\pi; area of △OED = \frac12\cdot6^2\sin60°=9\sqrt{3}. Therefore the area of the circular segment = 6\pi-9\sqrt{3}. Thus the shaded area = \frac{9\sqrt{3}}2-(6\pi-9\sqrt{3})=\frac{27\sqrt{3}}2-6\pi.
